summary: The article profiles seven local entrepreneurs who launched innovative businesses in the community after September 1, 2023. Their ventures span co-creative spaces, sustainable products, tech-enabled shoe repair, art installations, a home-chef platform, personalized retail and a makerspace. The piece argues these businesses prioritize community impact, sustainability and personal engagement alongside profit.
one_line: Profiles seven local entrepreneurs launching unique, community-focused business models between September and December 2023, from co-working and sustainability to art, food and retail.
key_facts: Anthony Weaver, a former tech consultant, launched the co-creative space 'Inventive Hub' on October 15, 2023 in the downtown area.

Inventive Hub runs on a subscription model and has an 'Idea-Investment' program that helps projects secure funding in exchange for a small share of future profits or a stake in the intellectual property.
Maria Gonzalez launched 'Eco-Nest' on November 1, 2023, a business built on sustainability that sells biodegradable packaging and upcycled home decor.
Eco-Nest collaborates with local artisans and runs workshops on sustainable living; Maria Gonzalez says it is about 'making a positive impact first and profits second'.
Jackson O'Reilly, a third-generation cobbler, merged his family's shoe repair business with technology on September 12, 2023, creating 'Heel the Sole'.
Heel the Sole's app lets customers schedule repairs, track progress and customize services, described as an industry first; business rose 50% in the first three months.
Lucy Nguyen, a local artist, founded 'Artify' on December 22, 2023, which curates temporary art installations in cafes, boutiques and bookstores.
Chris Martin launched 'DineMine' on September 8, 2023, a platform connecting home chefs with diners seeking authentic home-cooked meals.
Samantha Doyle launched 'Boutique Canvas' on October 2, 2023, blending data analytics with personal shoppers who suggest items based on purchasing history, preferences and moods.
Real estate developer Jake Hardin created 'Makerspace Loft' on November 18, 2023, offering specialized equipment and tools for makers, crafters and hardware startups.
Jake Hardin said: 'Imagine a world where a 3D printer is as accessible as a coffee maker.'
